newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INTERVIEW-Cerebos to up Indochina efforts.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Cerebos to up Indochina efforts.

text.p: Food-based Cerebos Pacific Ltd plans to push sales in Indochina and hopes higher consumption in these new markets will ensure double digit growth for 1997, managing director for Asia Michael Katayama said on Tuesday.
"We are now expanding the market for BRANDS products in China, Myanmar, Laos, and Vietnam and we are aiming to increase consumption there," Katayama told Reuters.
He said there was room to increase food consumption in these new markets and was optimistic they would prove as lucrative as China, where revenue has been growing at a rate of 20 percent a year.
That is the company's fastest rate and it is likely to continue at this brisk pace for the next few years, Katayam said.
He said Cerebos Pacific's Asia division now accounted for some 50 percent of revenue, and the highest growth was expected to come from Asian emerging markets.
Asked about the company's forecast for the next fiscal year, to end September 30, Katayama said: "I hope it will further continue to be double digit growth, more than 10 percent."
The company saw group revenue rise 11 percent in 1996 to Singapore $102.15 million for the 12 months to September.
Katayama said recent acquisitions in selected segments would also help boost profitability for the next fiscal year.
Cerebos Pacific's acquisition of 70 percent equity in Singapore-based Woh Hup Food Industries in late 1995 would enhance its position to export Asian spices and sauces, he said.
Asian sauces are a high growth segment in the region as well as in the West, as East-West cuisines become more popular.
A reversal of sales from Western markets into Asia, to meet changing tastes, will also be implemented soon.
"We will move some products like tomato sauce and coffee, sold only in Australia and New Zealand, to Asia," he said.
He said the new portfolio of products, as well as the BRANDS family of chicken essence products, ought to make a strong contribution this fiscal year.
In its December 1996 annual report, the company highlighted difficult conditions in New Zealand and Australia.
But it said the group made progress in selected product areas and would continue to build on these strengths this year.
